c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: Blocks sitting under `on button A pressed` are waiting. What are they waiting for?

A.text: For button A to be pressed

B.text: For the car to reach the floor

C.text: For the batteries to warm up

D.text: For the program to reach that line

c1.why: That block is an event handler. It sits still until the event happens — no matter where it is in the program.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: You download a program and put the car on the floor. Nobody touches a button. What is the program doing?

A.text: Nothing at all — it has finished

B.text: Driving slowly until someone stops it

C.text: Running, and waiting for a press

c2.why: The program is running the whole time. Waiting is something a running program does.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: A lift button does nothing until a finger touches it. Which block works the same way?
c3.why: Both wait for a person. The machine is already on and already running — it just has nothing to do yet.

r1.label: Q1
r1.prompt: You press A once and let go straight away. What do the wheels do?

B.text: They keep turning after you let go

C.text: They do not turn — one press is too short

D.text: They turn while your finger is down, then stop

r1.why: The block sets the motors going. Nothing in this program ever switches them off, so letting go changes nothing.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: You press A, wait two seconds, then press B. What does the car do?

B.text: Nothing — the two blocks cancel out

r2.why: Each press runs its own handler. B replaces what A was doing, so the car changes direction.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: In what order do these two things happen?

A.text: The face waits for the button, then shows

B.text: The face shows at once; the drive block waits for A

D.text: Both run at once when the program starts

r3.why: Loose blocks run at start-up. Blocks under an event block wait. They are not in a queue with each other.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: What does this program do the moment the car is switched on?

A.text: Nothing — there is no event block

r4.why: With no event block above it, this runs at start-up. And nothing stops it afterwards.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: This car takes off the instant it is switched on, before the student can put it down. Which change fixes it?

A.text: Move the drive block to the bottom

D.text: Put the drive block inside `on button A pressed`

d1.why: The drive block is loose, so it runs at start-up. Putting it under an event block makes it wait for a press.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: A pair say button B does nothing on their car. Looking at their blocks, what went wrong?

B.text: They need to press B harder

C.text: The second block still says A, not B

D.text: You cannot use both buttons in one program

d2.why: The two event blocks look almost identical — only the dropdown differs. Both say A here, so B has no job.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: You want the car to show a face at start-up, drive on A, and reverse on B. How many separate top-level pieces does that program need?

B.text: One — they all go in a row

b1.why: The face runs at start-up, and each button needs its own event block. Three pieces, and none of them run in order with the others.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: Put these in the order they happen when you get this program onto the floor: 1 press A · 2 download · 3 switch the car on · 4 put the car down
b2.why: Send the program, switch on, put it down, and only then press. Pressing while it is in your hand means a wheel spins in your fingers.
